variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Kubernetes is a control system for running containerized workloads across a cluster of machines. You declare an intended state through API objects: six application replicas, a stable service endpoint, a storage claim, or a rollout policy. Controllers continuously observe the cluster and take actions that move reality toward that declaration.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Declare desired state
pairs.detail: Submit a versioned manifest with identity, replicas, image digest, requests, probes, placement, configuration, and rollout policy.
pairs.explanation: Submit a versioned manifest with identity, replicas, image digest, requests, probes, placement, configuration, and rollout policy.

pairs.label: Persist and validate
pairs.detail: Authenticate, authorize, apply admission policy, validate the object, and persist cluster state through the control plane.
pairs.explanation: Authenticate, authorize, apply admission policy, validate the object, and persist cluster state through the control plane.

pairs.label: Schedule work
pairs.detail: Choose nodes that satisfy resource requests, affinity, taints, storage, topology, and policy constraints.
pairs.explanation: Choose nodes that satisfy resource requests, affinity, taints, storage, topology, and policy constraints.

pairs.label: Run and observe
pairs.detail: Pull images, start containers, mount configuration and volumes, execute probes, and report Pod status from each node.
pairs.explanation: Pull images, start containers, mount configuration and volumes, execute probes, and report Pod status from each node.

pairs.label: Reconcile again
pairs.detail: Replace missing replicas, progress rollouts, update endpoints, and retry until observed state matches the declaration or progress stops.
pairs.explanation: Replace missing replicas, progress rollouts, update endpoints, and retry until observed state matches the declaration or progress stops.

variants.hint:
Declare desired state: Submit a versioned manifest with identity, replicas, image digest, requests, probes, placement, configuration, and rollout policy.

Persist and validate: Authenticate, authorize, apply admission policy, validate the object, and persist cluster state through the control plane.

Schedule work: Choose nodes that satisfy resource requests, affinity, taints, storage, topology, and policy constraints.

Run and observe: Pull images, start containers, mount configuration and volumes, execute probes, and report Pod status from each node.

Reconcile again: Replace missing replicas, progress rollouts, update endpoints, and retry until observed state matches the declaration or progress stops.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Kubernetes is a control system for running containerized workloads across a cluster of machines. You declare an intended state through API objects: six application replicas, a stable service endpoint, a storage claim, or a rollout policy. Controllers continuously observe the cluster and take actions that move reality toward that declaration.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Pod
pairs.detail: One or more tightly coupled containers share a network namespace and volumes.
pairs.explanation: One or more tightly coupled containers share a network namespace and volumes. Pods are replaceable; their local filesystem and IP are normally ephemeral.

pairs.label: Deployment
pairs.detail: Owns ReplicaSets and progresses a versioned set of interchangeable Pods through rolling replacement.
pairs.explanation: Owns ReplicaSets and progresses a versioned set of interchangeable Pods through rolling replacement.

pairs.label: Service
pairs.detail: Selects ready endpoints behind a stable virtual address or name.
pairs.explanation: Selects ready endpoints behind a stable virtual address or name. It does not retry application operations or make them idempotent.

pairs.label: Job and CronJob
pairs.detail: Run work to completion under restart, retry, parallelism, deadline, and history policies.
pairs.explanation: Run work to completion under restart, retry, parallelism, deadline, and history policies. The job itself must tolerate repeated execution.

pairs.label: StatefulSet
pairs.detail: Provides ordered identities and per-replica storage claims, while the application still owns replication, quorum, backup, and recovery semantics.
pairs.explanation: Provides ordered identities and per-replica storage claims, while the application still owns replication, quorum, backup, and recovery semantics.

pairs.label: DaemonSet
pairs.detail: Runs a Pod on matching nodes for networking, storage, security, or telemetry functions and consumes capacity on every selected node.
pairs.explanation: Runs a Pod on matching nodes for networking, storage, security, or telemetry functions and consumes capacity on every selected node.

variants.hint:
Pod: One or more tightly coupled containers share a network namespace and volumes.

Deployment: Owns ReplicaSets and progresses a versioned set of interchangeable Pods through rolling replacement.

Service: Selects ready endpoints behind a stable virtual address or name.

Job and CronJob: Run work to completion under restart, retry, parallelism, deadline, and history policies.

StatefulSet: Provides ordered identities and per-replica storage claims, while the application still owns replication, quorum, backup, and recovery semantics.

DaemonSet: Runs a Pod on matching nodes for networking, storage, security, or telemetry functions and consumes capacity on every selected node.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Kubernetes is a control system for running containerized workloads across a cluster of machines. You declare an intended state through API objects: six application replicas, a stable service endpoint, a storage claim, or a rollout policy. Controllers continuously observe the cluster and take actions that move reality toward that declaration.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Identity and admission
pairs.detail: Use least-privilege RBAC and service accounts.
pairs.explanation: Use least-privilege RBAC and service accounts. Enforce image provenance, allowed registries, Pod security, required labels, and resource policy at admission.

pairs.label: Runtime isolation
pairs.detail: Run as a non-root user, drop capabilities, use read-only filesystems where practical, constrain syscalls, and isolate untrusted workloads strongly.
pairs.explanation: Run as a non-root user, drop capabilities, use read-only filesystems where practical, constrain syscalls, and isolate untrusted workloads strongly.

pairs.label: Network policy
pairs.detail: Default-deny ingress and egress, then allow identity- and purpose-specific paths.
pairs.explanation: Default-deny ingress and egress, then allow identity- and purpose-specific paths. Verify the selected network implementation enforces the policy.

pairs.label: Supply chain
pairs.detail: Pin digests, generate provenance and inventories, scan continuously, sign trusted artifacts, and make exception ownership explicit.
pairs.explanation: Pin digests, generate provenance and inventories, scan continuously, sign trusted artifacts, and make exception ownership explicit.

variants.hint:

Runtime isolation: Run as a non-root user, drop capabilities, use read-only filesystems where practical, constrain syscalls, and isolate untrusted workloads strongly.

Network policy: Default-deny ingress and egress, then allow identity- and purpose-specific paths.

Supply chain: Pin digests, generate provenance and inventories, scan continuously, sign trusted artifacts, and make exception ownership explicit.
